 Notes: Emmanuel McNeil-Warren’s ‘time to shine’ with Ronnie Hickman ruled out with concussion
 by
 Scott Petrak 
 November 13, 2026 
 BEREA — Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will have another milestone moment Sunday against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field.
 While McNeil-Warren has officially started three games and played about 40 percent of the defensive snaps this season as the third safety, the rookie from Toledo will make his first start in the base defense, filling in for Ronnie Hickman, who was ruled out Friday with a concussion. Hickman didn’t practice all week.
 Zone Coverage Podcast 
 “It feels good just to hear your name called, just be ready to step up when one of your teammates down,” McNeil-Warren, a second-round pick, said Friday. “Go out there, execute, play good, try to get them in for the team.”
 Advertisement 
 He’ll start alongside Grant Delpit at safety, with Daniel Thomas likely to move into McNeil-Warren’s spot as the No. 3.
 “E-Man, time to shine,” Delpit said. “We’ve been waiting for it. Listen, he has all the tools, great week of practice. He’s around the ball a lot, so I’m really excited for him to basically not come off the field and show what he could do.
 “Of course, we’re going to miss Rocket’s communication. He gets everybody lined up. He’s patrolling the middle of the field. So I know he’s been in E-Man’s ear this week to really try to get him going, get him a little head start.”
 McNeil-Warren’s most extended playing time of the season (54 of 57 snaps) came when Delpit sustained a concussion early against the Ravens. He’ll be in a starting role from Snap 1 against Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud and his talented group of receivers.
 “Just treat it like a regular game. Just another game,” McNeil-Warren said. “Just preparation from Monday through Friday.”
 Todd Monken goes back to Deshaun Watson, ‘anticipates’ him being the starter moving forward 
 Delpit said he’s stressing pre-snap communication.
 “He has all the physical tools to be a great player,” Delpit said. “As a rookie, it’s hard. Seeing a lot could be tough. Sometimes you want to see a little, but as a safety, you never have a choice, really. You’re going to have to communicate to everybody around you, everybody’s relying on you.”
 “Just try to follow Rocket’s footsteps with communication,” McNeil-Warren said. “Make sure everybody’s straight, everybody on point so the DBs will be all together and play fast together.”
 Coach Todd Monken saw McNeil-Warren’s evolution began on special teams.
 “You’ve seen tremendous growth,” he said. “Talk about range, talk about physicality, and he’s really got a high football IQ that I didn’t know when we took him. He’s got a really bright future.”
 BACK, BUT ALSO IN A BOOT 
 Rookie receiver Denzle Boston (toe) returned to practice after missing two days. He was limited and listed as questionable to face the Texans.
 He exited the locker room in a walking boot, which can be a precaution.
 “He came out there today and moved around. Moved around pretty good,” Monken said. “Went through our walk(through), took a full walk. But then when we got out there, we just limited his reps.
 “So we’ll have to see how he progresses tomorrow and then Sunday. But it’s trending in the right way.”
 Boston leads NFL rookies with 507 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns. He’s tied for fourth with 32 catches.
 If he can’t play, or is limited, veteran Jerry Jeudy would take on a bigger workload.
 “We’ll see. Hopefully he do play and hopefully he’s healthy,” said Jeudy, who had a key 30-yard catch last week vs. the Saints.
 INJURY REPORT 
 The Texans will be without a couple of important pieces from their defense and possibly a third.
 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (personal) and end Danielle Hunter (hamstring) were ruled out, while end Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) was listed as questionable after not practicing Friday. He was added to the report Thursday and was limited.
 Anderson leads the league with 9.5 sacks, Al-Shaair leads the Texans with 67 tackles and Hunter has four sacks.
 Houston also ruled out receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) and left guard Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder).
 ** The Browns ruled out fullback Michael Burton (calf).
 GOOD FOR HIM 
 Monken credited defensive end Jared Verse for capitalizing on the opportunity to meet with the team psychiatrist. Verse revealed that to reporters Thursday and said he believes it helped him clear a mental block, to which he attributed his no sacks through nine games.
 Jared Verse says he met with team psychiatrist, identified mental block, ‘very excited’ for Sunday 
 “It’s great that our players are willing to use the resources that are available, whether it’s Doc, whether it’s in the training room, whether it’s in the weight room, whether it’s all the coaches that we have at their disposal, because everyone in the building has a job for our players,” Monken said. “It’s a real credit to him. It’s been frustrating, right? He’s a really good football player, and all he’s trying to figure out is, ‘hey, where do we go from here, how do I fix it?’
 “I think once that happens, I think there’s going to be like an exhale. ‘Let’s get my first sack. Hey, I hit the quarterback,’ whatever that might be. And then I think you’re really going to see his season turn around. I really believe that.”
